# SKRSI

> SK Recursive SELF Improvement. The evidence-first improvement control plane
> for SK software lifecycle orchestration. SELF expands to Systematic
> Evaluation, Learning, and Feedback.

SKRSI measures software delivery, evaluates bounded experiments, records
lessons, and proposes safer improvements. It never grants authority, never
approves its own work, and never turns an observation into an actuation.

## Canonical naming (do not paraphrase)

The readable name is "SK Recursive SELF Improvement". The canonical expansion
is "SK Recursive Systematic Evaluation, Learning, and Feedback Improvement".

Noncanonical alternatives are retained only as naming history and must not
replace the canonical expansion: "Structured Evidence, Learning, and Feedback",
"Safe Experimentation, Learning, and Feedback", "Sustainable Evaluation,
Learning, and Feedback".

Runtime identifiers remain lowercase `skrsi`.

## Honest scope (do not overclaim)

- SKRSI produces typed observations, evaluations, and proposals. It does not
  own workflow state or authorization.
- It is currently documentation-first. Runtime components remain in SKCapstone
  until a governed extraction card moves them. This repository has no service
  and no network surface.
- Improvement is never inferred from throughput alone. Quality, security,
  reviewer independence, and missingness remain gates.
- An inconclusive experiment stays inconclusive. No model, agent, or operator
  can relabel it as successful.
- Maturity tier T0, not applicable, because the repository handles no key
  material. Version phase: Incubating.

## The SELF loop

1. Systematic: declared targets, cohorts, metrics, and stop rules.
2. Evaluation: compare evidence without inventing causality or hiding
   missingness.
3. Learning: preserve outcomes and lessons as versioned, attributable records.
4. Feedback: route bounded proposals back to the responsible lifecycle agent.

Flow: versioned target -> bounded metadata collector -> deterministic evaluator
-> independent review. A PASS becomes a feedback proposal that enters the
adopter's existing lifecycle gates. A FAIL or INCONCLUSIVE becomes a recorded
lesson. Both return to the target.

Every edge has one producer, one consumer, a bounded queue, a timeout, a retry
policy, a recovery owner, and immutable terminal evidence. Existing lifecycle
gates remain authoritative.

## Public contracts (metadata only)

- target-v2: bounded objective, measures, invariants, stop rules, expiry,
  rollback owner.
- event-envelope-v1: attributable metadata, lineage, hashes, redaction class.
- evaluation-v4: evaluation v3 plus evidence_class and an instrument
  self-description. A pass is impossible for synthetic evidence or when the
  instrument does not run production code. New producers use v4.
- evaluation-v3: independent participants, complete PASS metrics, quality
  gates, missingness, evidence-bound outcome. Immutable, superseded by v4.
- feedback-handoff-v1: routes a proposal to an existing authority without
  granting permission to act.

Compatibility is strict. Schema identifiers and files are immutable. Any field
addition, removal, type change, or constraint change requires a new schema
identifier and file. Unknown properties fail validation. Timestamps are RFC
3339 UTC. Digests are lowercase SHA-256 hex.

## Conformance levels (cumulative)

1. Record conformant: records validate; unknown versions and properties fail
   closed; digests, timestamps, identities, and redaction classes are valid.
2. Evidence conformant: digests reproducible; retries idempotent; conflicting
   replay rejected; missing, negative, null, and aborted outcomes stay visible.
3. Lifecycle conformant: producer and independent evaluator identities differ;
   a PASS carries numeric baseline and treatment values for every metric with
   no failed guardrail and no missingness entry; feedback is proposal-only;
   stop, expiry, rollback, and recovery are tested; no valid record grants
   merge, deployment, credential, or actuation power.

## In practice

Adoption is one caller workflow plus a target file. The reusable evaluate.yml
workflow runs the repo's bench on the PR head and at the base, builds an
evaluation v4 record, and upserts one PR comment per target. It is advisory:
it never fails the PR and must not be a required check. Outcome precedence is
regression, then fail, then inconclusive, then pass. The first code adopter
was the skmemory-retrieval target (November 2026); see the case study.
